final.memo:
Our investment thesis for the Company remains firmly on track. Since we reinitiated our position, management has successfully executed the complex integration of the KCS network, achieving more than $800 million in run-rate revenue synergies and significant operational efficiencies [D04], [D10]. These results are reflected in an 11% growth in core adjusted EPS for 2024 and management's constructive guidance of 12–18% growth for 2025 [D04], [D10].

While the current trade-policy environment and tariff threats represent an extrinsic risk factor, we believe the fundamental necessity of the trilateral North American rail network remains durable [D02], [D06]. As management has noted, these highly integrated supply chains are not easily substituted, and historical precedents suggest resilience in the face of similar trade disputes [D04], [D10]. The company's unique, scarce infrastructure continues to provide a significant competitive moat [D02], [D07].

We remain disciplined regarding the capital requirements of this business, noting that the substantial ongoing capex and debt levels require continued operational excellence [D02], [D10]. However, with the integration largely complete and the network's value proposition intact, the current valuation provides an attractive forward rate of return relative to the quality of the franchise [D05], [D09]. We view the market’s policy-driven uncertainty as a temporary sentiment factor rather than an impairment of the long-term intrinsic value of this dominant, high-quality railroad [D06], [D10].
